claim: A total of 17,179 known circRNAs were identified in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs).
source: A total of 17,179 known circRNAs were identified, with 66 of them exhibiting differential expression (GEO submission: GSE237597).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of circRNAs identified through transcriptome analysis.

claim: 66 circRNAs exhibited differential expression in PAHG-treated HUVECs compared to control.
source: A total of 17,179 known circRNAs were identified, with 66 of them exhibiting differential expression (GEO submission: GSE237597).
evidence: The manuscript states the number of differentially expressed circRNAs based on sequencing data.

claim: 48 circRNAs were upregulated in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: Specifically, 48 circRNAs were upregulated, whereas 18 were downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific counts of upregulated circRNAs and references a figure showing this data.

claim: 18 circRNAs were downregulated in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: Specifically, 48 circRNAs were upregulated, whereas 18 were downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific counts of downregulated circRNAs and references a figure showing this data.

claim: Approximately 66.65% of circRNAs were produced through reverse splicing of exons.
source: Furthermore, approximately 66.65% of circRNAs were found to be produced through reverse splicing of exons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The manuscript states a specific percentage based on analysis of circRNA biogenesis.

claim: circHMGCS1 (hsa_circ_0008621) is 899 nucleotides in length.
source: Among them, circHMGCS1 (hsa_circ_0008621, 899) nt in length, identified as circHMGCS1 in subsequent studies because of its host gene being HMGCS1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F; Liang et al., 2021) exhibited significant upregulation compared with the non-PAHG-treated condition (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the length of circHMGCS1.

claim: circHMGCS1 exhibited significant upregulation in PAHG-treated HUVECs compared to non-PAHG-treated condition.
source: Among them, circHMGCS1 (hsa_circ_0008621, 899) nt in length, identified as circHMGCS1 in subsequent studies because of its host gene being HMGCS1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F; Liang et al., 2021) exhibited significant upregulation compared with the non-PAHG-treated condition (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript states upregulation and references qRT-PCR validation data in Figure 1B.

claim: circHMGCS1 originates from exons 2–7 of the HMGCS1 gene.
source: This observation confirms the origin of circHMGCS1 from exons 2–7 of the HMGCS1 gene (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, H).
evidence: The manuscript confirms the exon origin through Sanger sequencing and references supporting figures.

claim: circHMGCS1 is predominantly expressed in the cytoplasm of HUVECs.
source: The qRT-PCR analysis of nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA revealed the predominant cytoplasmic expression of circHMGCS1 in HUVECs (Figure 1G).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR analysis of subcellular fractionation showing cytoplasmic localization.

claim: circHMGCS1 has a stable half-life exceeding 24 hours.
source: qRT-PCR also demonstrated that circHMGCS1 displayed a stable half-life exceeding 24 hr, whereas the linear transcript HMGCS1 mRNA had a half-life of less than 8 hr (Figure 1H).
evidence: The manuscript reports actinomycin D treatment experiments measuring RNA stability over time.

claim: HMGCS1 mRNA has a half-life of less than 8 hours.
source: qRT-PCR also demonstrated that circHMGCS1 displayed a stable half-life exceeding 24 hr, whereas the linear transcript HMGCS1 mRNA had a half-life of less than 8 hr (Figure 1H).
evidence: The manuscript reports actinomycin D treatment experiments measuring RNA stability over time.

claim: circHMGCS1 is resistant to RNase R digestion.
source: Furthermore, circHMGCS1 exhibited resistance to digestion by ribonuclease R (an exonuclease that selectively degrades linear RNA Xiao and Wilusz, 2019, also known as RNase R), whereas linear HMGCS1 mRNA was easily degraded upon RNase R treatment (Figure 1I).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNase R treatment experiments showing differential stability between circular and linear RNA.

claim: Linear HMGCS1 mRNA is easily degraded by RNase R treatment.
source: Furthermore, circHMGCS1 exhibited resistance to digestion by ribonuclease R (an exonuclease that selectively degrades linear RNA Xiao and Wilusz, 2019, also known as RNase R), whereas linear HMGCS1 mRNA was easily degraded upon RNase R treatment (Figure 1I).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNase R treatment experiments showing differential stability between circular and linear RNA.

claim: Overexpression of circHMGCS1 increased its level nearly 60-fold compared to linear transcripts.
source: We found that circHMGCS1 was successfully overexpressed in HUVECs without significant changes in HMGCS1 mRNA expression, and the level of the circular transcripts increased nearly 60-fold than the level of the linear transcripts (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR measurements of overexpression efficiency.

claim: Overexpression of circHMGCS1 does not significantly change HMGCS1 mRNA expression.
source: We found that circHMGCS1 was successfully overexpressed in HUVECs without significant changes in HMGCS1 mRNA expression, and the level of the circular transcripts increased nearly 60-fold than the level of the linear transcripts (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR measurements showing no effect on host gene expression.

claim: Overexpression of circHMGCS1 stimulates the expression of adhesion molecules VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1.
source: Further experiments demonstrated that the overexpression of circHMGCS1 stimulated the expression of adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 2B, C), suggesting that circHMGCS1 is involved in VED promotion.
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot and qRT-PCR data showing increased adhesion molecule expression.

claim: circHMGCS1 overexpression further decreases NO levels in PAHG-stimulated HUVECs.
source: NO levels were significantly decreased after PAHG stimulation for 24 hr, and circHMGCS1 overexpression further decreased NO levels (Figure 2D), indicating that increased circHMGCS1 expression inhibits endothelial diastolic function.
evidence: The manuscript reports NO content measurements showing additive effect of circHMGCS1 overexpression.

claim: Upregulated circHMGCS1 expression further decreases ENOS activity in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: ENOS activity was inhibited by PAHG, and upregulated circHMGCS1 expression further decreased ENOS activity (Figure 2E).
evidence: The manuscript reports ENOS activity assay results showing additive inhibitory effect.

claim: Overexpression of circHMGCS1 enhances PAHG-induced ROS generation.
source: The overexpression of circHMGCS1 enhanced PAHG-induced ROS generation (Figure 2F), increasing oxidative stress in endothelial cells.
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements showing increased ROS levels.

claim: 98 significantly differentially expressed miRNAs were identified in PAHG-stimulated HUVECs.
source: The deep sequencing analysis revealed 98 significantly differentially expressed miRNAs (Figure 3A and B, GEO submission: GSE237295).
evidence: The manuscript reports miRNA sequencing results.

claim: Four candidate miRNAs (MIR4521, MIR3143, MIR98-5P, and MIR181A-2–3P) were identified as potential targets of circHMGCS1.
source: We then used the miRanda database and ceRNA theory to obtain four candidate miRNAs (MIR4521, MIR3143, MIR98-5P, and MIR181A-2–3 P; Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The manuscript reports bioinformatics prediction combined with sequencing data.

claim: All four candidate miRNAs (MIR4521, MIR3143, MIR98-5P, and MIR181A-2–3P) were downregulated in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: qRT-PCR confirmed that all four miRNAs were downregulated (Figure 3E).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR validation of miRNA expression levels.

claim: MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibit adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) expression in HUVECs.
source: Relative to the other three miRNAs, MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibited adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) expression in HUVECs (Figure 3F and G), making it a suitable candidate for further endothelial function studies.
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data comparing effects of different miRNA mimics.

claim: Enhanced MIR4521 levels effectively restore PAHG-induced reductions in NO content in HUVECs.
source: Enhanced MIR4521 levels effectively restored PAHG-induced reductions in NO content and ENOS activity in HUEVCs, while MIR4521 inhibition led to opposite results (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: The manuscript reports NO content measurements with MIR4521 mimics treatment.

claim: Enhanced MIR4521 levels effectively restore PAHG-induced reductions in ENOS activity in HUVECs.
source: Enhanced MIR4521 levels effectively restored PAHG-induced reductions in NO content and ENOS activity in HUEVCs, while MIR4521 inhibition led to opposite results (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: The manuscript reports ENOS activity measurements with MIR4521 mimics treatment.

claim: MIR4521 inhibition leads to opposite results compared to MIR4521 mimics on NO content and ENOS activity.
source: Enhanced MIR4521 levels effectively restored PAHG-induced reductions in NO content and ENOS activity in HUEVCs, while MIR4521 inhibition led to opposite results (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: The manuscript reports measurements with MIR4521 inhibitor showing opposite effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibit PAHG-induced expression of ROS.
source: whereas MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibited PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3J), whereas the MIR4521 inhibitor increased the PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3K and L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements showing ROS reduction with MIR4521 mimics.

claim: MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibit PAHG-induced expression of adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1).
source: whereas MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibited PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3J), whereas the MIR4521 inhibitor increased the PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3K and L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot and qRT-PCR data showing reduced adhesion molecule expression.

claim: MIR4521 inhibitor increases PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1).
source: whereas MIR4521 mimics significantly inhibited PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3J), whereas the MIR4521 inhibitor increased the PAHG-induced expression of ROS and adhesion molecules (VCAM1, ICAM1, and ET-1; Figure 3K and L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports measurements showing increased ROS and adhesion molecules with MIR4521 inhibitor.

claim: Overexpression of circHMGCS1 reduces the expression level of MIR4521.
source: As displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B, the overexpression of circHMGCS1 reduced the expression level of MIR4521, whereas knockdown of circHMGCS1 resulted in an upregulation of MIR4521.
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR measurements showing inverse relationship between circHMGCS1 and MIR4521.

claim: Knockdown of circHMGCS1 results in upregulation of MIR4521.
source: As displayed in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B, the overexpression of circHMGCS1 reduced the expression level of MIR4521, whereas knockdown of circHMGCS1 resulted in an upregulation of MIR4521.
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR measurements showing inverse relationship between circHMGCS1 and MIR4521.

claim: Co-transfection of MIR4521 mimics with circHMGCS1 luciferase reporter gene reduces luciferase activity.
source: The co-transfection of MIR4521 mimics with the circHMGCS1 luciferase reporter gene in HEK293T cells, reducing luciferase activity; mutations in the binding sites between circHMGCS1 and MIR4521 abrogated the effect of MIR4521 mimics on the activity of the circHMGCS1 luciferase reporter gene mutant (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports dual-luciferase assay results demonstrating direct binding.

claim: Mutations in the binding sites between circHMGCS1 and MIR4521 abrogate the effect of MIR4521 mimics on luciferase activity.
source: The co-transfection of MIR4521 mimics with the circHMGCS1 luciferase reporter gene in HEK293T cells, reducing luciferase activity; mutations in the binding sites between circHMGCS1 and MIR4521 abrogated the effect of MIR4521 mimics on the activity of the circHMGCS1 luciferase reporter gene mutant (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports dual-luciferase assay results with mutant constructs showing specificity of binding.

claim: MIR4521 facilitates the association of AGO2 with circHMGCS1 in HUVECs.
source: Furthermore, AGO2 immunoprecipitation in HUVECs transfected with MIR4521 or its mutants demonstrated that MIR4521 facilitates the association of AGO2 with circHMGCS1 in HUVECs (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA immunoprecipitation results showing AGO2-mediated interaction.

claim: MIR4521 captures endogenous circHMGCS1 in biotinylated pull-down assays.
source: The qRT-PCR results revealed that MIR4521 captured endogenous circHMGCS1, and the negative control with a disrupting putative binding sequence failed to coprecipitate circHMGCS1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports biotin pull-down assay results demonstrating direct interaction.

claim: Biotin-labeled circHMGCS1 effectively captures both MIR4521 and AGO2.
source: Consistently, the use of biotin-labeled circHMGCS1 effectively captured both MIR4521 and AGO2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports reciprocal pull-down assay results confirming the interaction.

claim: MIR4521 and circHMGCS1 colocalize in the cytoplasm.
source: Moreover, the RNA-FISH assay showed colocalization of MIR4521 and circHMGCS1 in the cytoplasm (Figure 4D).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-FISH imaging showing spatial colocalization.

claim: MIR4521 sponges significantly promote PAHG-induced reduction in NO content.
source: Notably, MIR4521 sponges significantly promoted the PAHG-induced reduction in NO content and ENOS activity. Under this condition, increased circHMGCS1 expression did not interfere with the changes in NO content and ENOS activity (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments with MIR4521 sponges showing loss of circHMGCS1 effect.

claim: Increased circHMGCS1 expression does not interfere with changes in NO content when MIR4521 is sponged.
source: Notably, MIR4521 sponges significantly promoted the PAHG-induced reduction in NO content and ENOS activity. Under this condition, increased circHMGCS1 expression did not interfere with the changes in NO content and ENOS activity (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments demonstrating MIR4521 is required for circHMGCS1 function.

claim: MIR4521 sponges elevate ROS expression in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: Moreover, MIR4521 sponges elevated ROS expression in PAHG treated HUVECs, whereas no further additional effect on ROS expression was observed upon the overexpression of circHMGCS1 when MIR4521 was sponged (Figure 4G).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements with MIR4521 sponges.

claim: circHMGCS1 fails to stimulate expression of adhesion molecules when MIR4521 is sponged.
source: Further evaluation of endothelial functional molecules revealed that circHMGCS1 failed to stimulate the expression of these factors when MIR4521 was sponged (Figure 4H–J).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot and qRT-PCR data showing loss of circHMGCS1 effect with MIR4521 sponges.

claim: MIR4521 mimics reverse the reduction in NO content induced by circHMGCS1 overexpression.
source: Furthermore, the reduction in NO content and ENOS activity induced by circHMGCS1 overexpression was reversed by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4K and L), and the circHMGCS1-mediated increase in ROS content was inhibited by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4M).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing MIR4521 can counteract circHMGCS1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics reverse the reduction in ENOS activity induced by circHMGCS1 overexpression.
source: Furthermore, the reduction in NO content and ENOS activity induced by circHMGCS1 overexpression was reversed by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4K and L), and the circHMGCS1-mediated increase in ROS content was inhibited by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4M).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing MIR4521 can counteract circHMGCS1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics inhibit the circHMGCS1-mediated increase in ROS content.
source: Furthermore, the reduction in NO content and ENOS activity induced by circHMGCS1 overexpression was reversed by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4K and L), and the circHMGCS1-mediated increase in ROS content was inhibited by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4M).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements showing MIR4521 can counteract circHMGCS1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics significantly ameliorate the increased expression of adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) in circHMGCS1-transfected HUVECs.
source: Furthermore, the expression of adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) was increased in circHMGCS1-transfected HUVECs, and this effect was significantly ameliorated by MIR4521 mimics (Figure 4N–P).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot and qRT-PCR data showing rescue of adhesion molecule expression.

claim: MIR4521 agomir significantly decreases body weight in diabetic mice compared to untreated diabetic mice.
source: Compared with to non-diabetic WT (Control) mice, DM mice exhibited a significant increase in body weight, upon MIR4521 agomir application, the body weight of diabetic mice significantly decreased compared with the untreated diabetic mice (Figure 5A), and elevated fasting blood glucose levels in DM mice were likewise substantially inhibited (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports body weight measurements over time in different treatment groups.

claim: MIR4521 agomir substantially inhibits elevated fasting blood glucose levels in diabetic mice.
source: Compared with to non-diabetic WT (Control) mice, DM mice exhibited a significant increase in body weight, upon MIR4521 agomir application, the body weight of diabetic mice significantly decreased compared with the untreated diabetic mice (Figure 5A), and elevated fasting blood glucose levels in DM mice were likewise substantially inhibited (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports fasting blood glucose measurements over time in different treatment groups.

claim: Combined treatment of circHMGCS1 and MIR4521 agomir does not significantly affect body weight and blood glucose levels.
source: By contrast, the combined treatment of circHMGCS1 and MIR4521 agomir did not significantly affect the body weight and blood glucose levels.
evidence: The manuscript reports measurements showing circHMGCS1 negates MIR4521 effects.

claim: MIR4521 agomir considerably enhances glucose tolerance in diabetic mice.
source: OGTT and ITT experiments demonstrated that MIR4521 agomir considerably enhanced glucose tolerance and insulin resistance in diabetic mice (Figure 5C and D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The manuscript reports OGTT and ITT results showing improved metabolic parameters.

claim: MIR4521 agomir considerably enhances insulin resistance in diabetic mice.
source: OGTT and ITT experiments demonstrated that MIR4521 agomir considerably enhanced glucose tolerance and insulin resistance in diabetic mice (Figure 5C and D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The manuscript reports OGTT and ITT results showing improved metabolic parameters.

claim: MIR4521 agomir restores abnormal blood lipid levels in diabetic mice.
source: Blood lipid biochemistry analysis revealed that MIR4521 agomir restored abnormal blood lipid levels in diabetic mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: The manuscript reports serum lipid measurements showing improvement with MIR4521 treatment.

claim: circHMGCS1 negates the inhibitory effect of MIR4521 on diabetes development.
source: Notably, the abundant presence of circHMGCS1 in the body can negate the inhibitory effect of MIR4521 on diabetes development.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes results from combined treatment experiments showing antagonistic relationship.

claim: MIR4521 agomir markedly improves impaired acetylcholine-induced vascular relaxation response in the thoracic aorta of diabetic mice.
source: A significant impairment in acetylcholine (Ach)-induced vascular relaxation response in the thoracic aorta of diabetic mice was markedly improved by MIR4521 agomir, emphasizing the critical involvement of MIR4521 in vascular relaxation.
evidence: The manuscript reports ex vivo vascular function measurements showing improved relaxation.

claim: circHMGCS1 inhibits the protective function of MIR4521 on vascular relaxation.
source: Conversely, circHMGCS1 inhibited the protective function of MIR4521 on vascular relaxation (Figure 5E).
evidence: The manuscript reports vascular function measurements showing circHMGCS1 antagonizes MIR4521 effects.

claim: Diabetic mice display a significant increase in systolic blood pressure compared to normal mice.
source: Meanwhile, diabetic mice displayed a significant increase in SBP compared with normal mice, which was significantly restrained by MIR4521 agomir treatment.
evidence: The manuscript reports blood pressure measurements showing diabetes-induced hypertension.

claim: MIR4521 agomir treatment significantly restrains the increase in systolic blood pressure in diabetic mice.
source: Meanwhile, diabetic mice displayed a significant increase in SBP compared with normal mice, which was significantly restrained by MIR4521 agomir treatment.
evidence: The manuscript reports blood pressure measurements showing MIR4521 reduces hypertension.

claim: The beneficial effect of MIR4521 agomir on systolic blood pressure is nullified in the presence of circHMGCS1.
source: Nevertheless, this beneficial effect was nullified in the presence of circHMGCS1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: The manuscript reports blood pressure measurements showing circHMGCS1 negates MIR4521 effects.

claim: MIR4521 agomir inhibits intimal thickening and smooth muscle cell proliferation in diabetic mice.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 agomir inhibited intimal thickening and smooth muscle cell proliferation in diabetic mice, whereas upregulation of circHMGCS1 abrogated this effect (Figure 5G).
evidence: The manuscript reports H&E staining results showing improved vascular morphology.

claim: Upregulation of circHMGCS1 abrogates the effect of MIR4521 agomir on intimal thickening and smooth muscle cell proliferation.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 agomir inhibited intimal thickening and smooth muscle cell proliferation in diabetic mice, whereas upregulation of circHMGCS1 abrogated this effect (Figure 5G).
evidence: The manuscript reports H&E staining results showing circHMGCS1 negates MIR4521 effects.

claim: MIR4521 agomir treatment increases NO content in the thoracic aorta of diabetic mice.
source: Compared with the control group, the NO level decreased in the thoracic aorta of diabetic mice; however, MIR4521 agomir treatment increased its content (Figure 5H).
evidence: The manuscript reports NO content measurements in vascular tissue.

claim: MIR4521 treatment effectively enhances Enos activity in diabetic mice.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 treatment effectively enhanced Enos activity (Figure 5I), whereas circHMGCS1 hindered MIR4521 regulatory function on NO content and ENOS activity.
evidence: The manuscript reports ENOS activity measurements in vascular tissue.

claim: circHMGCS1 hinders MIR4521 regulatory function on NO content and ENOS activity.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 treatment effectively enhanced Enos activity (Figure 5I), whereas circHMGCS1 hindered MIR4521 regulatory function on NO content and ENOS activity.
evidence: The manuscript reports measurements showing circHMGCS1 antagonizes MIR4521 effects.

claim: MIR4521 reduces ROS production in blood vessels of diabetic mice.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 reduced ROS production in the blood vessels (Figure 5J and K) and inhibited the expression of endothelial adhesion molecules (Icam1, Et-1, and Vcam1; Figure 5L).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements in vascular tissue.

claim: MIR4521 inhibits the expression of endothelial adhesion molecules (Icam1, Et-1, and Vcam1) in diabetic mice.
source: Furthermore, MIR4521 reduced ROS production in the blood vessels (Figure 5J and K) and inhibited the expression of endothelial adhesion molecules (Icam1, Et-1, and Vcam1; Figure 5L).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot measurements of adhesion molecules in vascular tissue.

claim: In the presence of circHMGCS1, the effect of MIR4521 on ROS and adhesion molecules is abrogated.
source: Nonetheless, in the presence of circHMGCS1, the effect of MIR4521 was abrogated.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes results showing circHMGCS1 negates MIR4521 effects on multiple parameters.

claim: Elevated arginase activity in endothelial cells contributes to diabetes-induced vascular endothelial dysfunction.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated the involvement of elevated arginase activity in diabetes-induced VED. Arginase can modulate the production of NO synthesized by ENOS through competitive utilization of the shared substrate L-arginine (Jung et al., 2010; Romero et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies establishing the role of arginase in VED.

claim: Arginase modulates NO production by ENOS through competitive utilization of L-arginine.
source: Arginase can modulate the production of NO synthesized by ENOS through competitive utilization of the shared substrate L-arginine (Jung et al., 2010; Romero et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies explaining the mechanism of arginase action.

claim: MIR4521 possesses the capability to bind to the 3' untranslated region of ARG1 in both human and mouse genomes.
source: Moreover, MIR4521 possesses the capability to bind to the 3' untranslated region of ARG1 in both human and mouse genomes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports bioinformatics prediction of binding sites.

claim: ARG1 protein expression is increased in the aorta of diabetic mice.
source: The protein expression of Arg1 was increased in the aorta of diabetic mice and PAHG-treated HUVECs (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data showing increased ARG1 in diabetes.

claim: ARG1 protein expression is increased in PAHG-treated HUVECs.
source: The protein expression of Arg1 was increased in the aorta of diabetic mice and PAHG-treated HUVECs (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data showing increased ARG1 in PAHG treatment.

claim: Overexpression of MIR4521 reduces the luciferase activities of the wild-type ARG1 3'-UTR reporter vector.
source: The overexpression of MIR4521 reduced the luciferase activities of the WT reporter vector but not the MUT reporter vector (Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript reports dual-luciferase assay results demonstrating direct targeting.

claim: Overexpression of MIR4521 does not reduce the luciferase activities of the mutant ARG1 3'-UTR reporter vector.
source: The overexpression of MIR4521 reduced the luciferase activities of the WT reporter vector but not the MUT reporter vector (Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript reports dual-luciferase assay results showing specificity of targeting.

claim: MIR4521 mimics recover reduced levels of NO triggered by ARG1 overexpression.
source: MIR4521 mimics recovered the reduced levels of NO and the compromised activity of ENOS triggered by ARG1 overexpression (Figure 6D and E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing MIR4521 counteracts ARG1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics recover compromised activity of ENOS triggered by ARG1 overexpression.
source: MIR4521 mimics recovered the reduced levels of NO and the compromised activity of ENOS triggered by ARG1 overexpression (Figure 6D and E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing MIR4521 counteracts ARG1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics inhibit the upregulation in ROS levels induced by ARG1 overexpression.
source: Meanwhile, it inhibited the upregulation in ROS levels induced by ARG1 overexpression (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements showing MIR4521 counteracts ARG1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics reverse the promotional effect of ARG1 on mRNA and protein expression of adhesion molecules in vitro.
source: The rescue experiment results demonstrated that MIR4521 mimics reversed the promotional effect of ARG1 on the mRNA and protein expression of adhesion molecules in vitro (Figure 6G and H).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot and qRT-PCR data showing MIR4521 counteracts ARG1 effects.

claim: MIR4521 mimics repress ARG1 transcription and protein expression.
source: MIR4521 mimics repressed ARG1 transcription and protein expression, whereas MIR4521 inhibition upregulated ARG1 expression (Figure 6I–K).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR and western blot data showing MIR4521 regulates ARG1.

claim: MIR4521 inhibition upregulates ARG1 expression.
source: MIR4521 mimics repressed ARG1 transcription and protein expression, whereas MIR4521 inhibition upregulated ARG1 expression (Figure 6I–K).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR and western blot data showing inverse regulation.

claim: circHMGCS1 overexpression significantly promotes ARG1 transcription and protein expression during PAHG treatment.
source: circHMGCS1 overexpression significantly further promoted ARG1 transcription and protein expression during the PAHG treatment (Figure 6L and M), confirming the regulatory function of circHMGCS1 in VED-related ARG1 expression.
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR and western blot data showing circHMGCS1 upregulates ARG1.

claim: MIR4521 overexpression counteracts the effects of circHMGCS1 on ARG1 mRNA and protein expression.
source: The mRNA and protein levels of ARG1 were significantly increased when HUVECs were transfected with circHMGCS1. However, MIR4521 overexpression counteracted the effects of circHMGCS1 on ARG1 mRNA and protein expression (Figure 6N and O).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing MIR4521 antagonizes circHMGCS1 effects on ARG1.

claim: Knockdown of circHMGCS1 reduces ARG1 expression in HUVECs.
source: Conversely, knockdown of circHMGCS1 reduced ARG1 expression and increased MIR4521 expression in HUVECs (Figure 6P and Q and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports qRT-PCR and western blot data showing inverse relationship.

claim: Inhibition of MIR4521 using a MIR4521 sponge further increases ARG1 expression under PAHG treatment.
source: Besides, the inhibition of MIR4521 using a MIR4521 sponge in HUVECs further increased ARG1 expression under the PAHG treatment. Notably, elevated circHMGCS1 expression did not affect ARG1 regulation (Figure 6R).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data showing MIR4521 is required for circHMGCS1 to regulate ARG1.

claim: Elevated circHMGCS1 expression does not affect ARG1 regulation when MIR4521 is sponged.
source: Besides, the inhibition of MIR4521 using a MIR4521 sponge in HUVECs further increased ARG1 expression under the PAHG treatment. Notably, elevated circHMGCS1 expression did not affect ARG1 regulation (Figure 6R).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data showing MIR4521 is required for circHMGCS1 function.

claim: circHMGCS1 overexpression dampens the function of MIR4521 agomir on Arg1 in diabetic mice.
source: Moreover, compared with diabetic mice, circHMGCS1 overexpression dampened the function of MIR4521 agomir on Arg1 (Figure 6S).
evidence: The manuscript reports western blot data from mouse aorta showing circHMGCS1 antagonizes MIR4521 effects.

claim: ARG1 shRNA mitigates the effects of PAHG on NO content in endothelial cells.
source: ARG1 shRNA mitigated the effects of PAHG on NO content and ENOS activity (Figure 7A and B), and inhibited PAHG-induced ROS in endothelial cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing ARG1 knockdown protects against PAHG effects.

claim: ARG1 shRNA mitigates the effects of PAHG on ENOS activity in endothelial cells.
source: ARG1 shRNA mitigated the effects of PAHG on NO content and ENOS activity (Figure 7A and B), and inhibited PAHG-induced ROS in endothelial cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: The manuscript reports rescue experiments showing ARG1 knockdown protects against PAHG effects.

claim: ARG1 shRNA inhibits PAHG-induced ROS in endothelial cells.
source: ARG1 shRNA mitigated the effects of PAHG on NO content and ENOS activity (Figure 7A and B), and inhibited PAHG-induced ROS in endothelial cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: The manuscript reports DHE fluorescence measurements showing ARG1 knockdown reduces ROS.

claim: ARG1 shRNA significantly reduces the elevated expression of adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) induced by PAHG.
source: Additionally, ARG1 shRNA significantly reduced the elevated expression of adhesion molecules (ICAM1, VCAM1, and ET-1) induced by PAHG (Figure 7D and E).
